identity.name: Azure Conditional-Access & Mailbox-Rule Persistence (SIM-ITDR-019)
identity.summary: An identity actor weakens the Entra ID conditional-access posture (adds/updates/deletes a CA policy) then plants a covert inbox-rule that auto-forwards mail externally. azure_audit_emitter streams shape-true Azure Audit Log + O365 records into the operator collector so XSIAM's rule-based Analytics alerts and the ABIOCs fire on the persistence chain.
identity.description: Validates the XSIAM 'Azure Audit Log' data-source Analytics alerts 'Azure conditional access policy creation or modification' and 'Azure mailbox rule creation'. The technique models a common cloud-identity persistence chain (T1556 Modify Authentication Process → T1114.003 Email Forwarding Rule): an attacker who has obtained a privileged/service-principal identity relaxes the conditional-access enforcement that would otherwise block their session, then establishes covert collection via an external auto-forwarding inbox rule. The card ships the two Analytics alerts as rule-based XQL bodies plus two auto-tuned ABIOCs (deviation from the learned per-admin CA-change / per-mailbox inbox-rule baseline) and a correlation rule that stitches the CA weakening and the mail-rule creation into a single Azure identity-persistence incident on the shared initiating identity.

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-ITDR-019 — azure_audit_emitter drives the Azure Audit Log + O365 audit emission for the CA-policy and inbox-rule persistence legs.

prerequisites.description: An operator-supplied HTTP log collector is wired into Cortex XSIAM as the Azure Audit Log / Microsoft 365 third-party source so the emitted records land in msft_azure_audit and msft_o365_audit.

payload.code:
# Emit the two-stage Azure identity-persistence chain via the analytics streamer.
# Leg 1: conditional-access policy modification -> msft_azure_audit
# Leg 2: external auto-forwarding inbox rule creation -> msft_o365_audit
set -euo pipefail
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/itdr-019.yml --live

input_variables.name: COLLECTOR_URL
input_variables.description: Operator-supplied HTTP collector wired into XSIAM as the Azure Audit Log / M365 source.

input_variables.name: TARGET_USER
input_variables.description: Initiating identity whose Azure Audit Log / mailbox the synthetic persistence records are attributed to.

expected_artifacts.description: Azure Audit Log record for an Add/Update/Delete conditional access policy operation attributed to the initiating identity.
O365 audit record for a New-InboxRule / Set-InboxRule with an external ForwardTo/RedirectTo target.

abiocs.name: Conditional-access policy weakened off the learned admin-change baseline
abiocs.description: Auto-tuned ABIOC — an identity or service principal whose learned baseline is a low, stable cadence of conditional-access changes suddenly updates or deletes CA policies (relaxing MFA / device-compliance / location enforcement). Fires on the deviation from the per-actor CA-change baseline, anchored to the identity causality chain rather than any single known-bad operation.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = msft_azure_audit
| filter loggedByService = "Conditional Access" and activityDisplayName in ("Update conditional access policy", "Delete conditional access policy")
| alter actor = initiatedBy_user_userPrincipalName, actor_app = initiatedBy_app_displayName, policy = targetResources_displayName
| comp count() as policy_changes by actor, actor_app, policy
| filter policy_changes >= 1
| fields actor, actor_app, policy, policy_changes
abiocs.causality_anchor: The learned per-identity conditional-access change baseline (which admins/service principals normally modify CA policy, at what cadence); the ABIOC anchors its deviation to the initiating identity's audit chain.

abiocs.name: External mailbox forwarding rule off the learned inbox-rule baseline
abiocs.description: Auto-tuned ABIOC — a mailbox that has never (or rarely) created client-side inbox rules suddenly creates a rule that forwards or redirects mail to an external recipient. Fires on the deviation from the per-mailbox inbox-rule baseline, anchored to the identity that follows the conditional-access weakening in the same persistence chain.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = msft_o365_audit
| filter Operation in ("New-InboxRule", "Set-InboxRule")
| alter mailbox = UserId, rule_name = RuleName, forward_to = ForwardTo, redirect_to = RedirectTo
| filter forward_to != null or redirect_to != null
| comp count() as external_forward_rules by mailbox, rule_name, forward_to, redirect_to
| filter external_forward_rules >= 1
| fields mailbox, rule_name, forward_to, redirect_to, external_forward_rules
abiocs.causality_anchor: The learned per-mailbox inbox-rule baseline (whether this mailbox normally auto-forwards externally); anchored to the same initiating identity as the preceding conditional-access change.

xql_queries.name: Azure conditional access policy creation or modification
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_azure_audit
| filter category = "Policy" and loggedByService = "Conditional Access"
| filter activityDisplayName in ("Add conditional access policy", "Update conditional access policy", "Delete conditional access policy")
| alter actor = initiatedBy_user_userPrincipalName, actor_app = initiatedBy_app_displayName, policy = targetResources_displayName
| comp count() as change_count by actor, actor_app, policy, activityDisplayName
| filter change_count >= 1
| fields actor, actor_app, policy, activityDisplayName, change_count

xql_queries.name: Azure mailbox rule creation
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_o365_audit
| filter Operation in ("New-InboxRule", "Set-InboxRule", "New-TransportRule")
| alter mailbox = UserId, rule_name = RuleName, forward_to = ForwardTo, redirect_to = RedirectTo
| filter forward_to != null or redirect_to != null or DeleteMessage = "True"
| comp count() as rule_events by mailbox, rule_name, Operation, forward_to, redirect_to
| filter rule_events >= 1
| fields mailbox, rule_name, Operation, forward_to, redirect_to, rule_events

xql_queries.name: Azure Audit Log persistence signals landed in datasets
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_azure_audit
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900) and loggedByService = "Conditional Access"
| alter signal = "ca_policy_change"
| fields signal, _time
| union (dataset = msft_o365_audit | filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900) and Operation in ("New-InboxRule", "Set-InboxRule") | alter signal = "inbox_rule_create" | fields signal, _time)
| comp count() as observed_events by signal
| filter observed_events >= 1
| fields signal, observed_events

correlation_rules.name: Azure Identity Persistence — CA policy weakening then covert mail rule
correlation_rules.logic: Fires when analytics `Azure conditional access policy creation or modification` (or abioc `Conditional-access policy weakened off the learned admin-change baseline`) and analytics `Azure mailbox rule creation` (or abioc `External mailbox forwarding rule off the learned inbox-rule baseline`) both fire for the same initiating identity within a 30-minute window. Stitches the two legs into one two-stage Azure identity-persistence incident: the actor first relaxes conditional-access enforcement, then plants a covert external mail-forwarding rule for collection.

use_cases.name: Azure identity persistence — conditional-access weakening and covert mailbox forwarding
use_cases.description: POV use case proving the Azure Audit Log Analytics alerts and their auto-tuned ABIOCs fire on a two-stage Entra ID / M365 persistence chain, and that XSIAM correlation stitches both legs into a single incident on the shared initiating identity.

test_cases.objective: The 'Azure conditional access policy creation or modification' Analytics alert (and the CA-weakening ABIOC) fire when a CA policy is updated/deleted off the learned admin-change baseline.
preconditions: The Azure Audit Log source is ingesting into msft_azure_audit.
Cortex has learned a per-identity conditional-access change baseline.
steps: Run azure_audit_emitter to stream a conditional-access policy update/delete record.
Observe the Analytics alert and the CA-weakening ABIOC fire on the initiating identity.
success_criteria: Analytics `Azure conditional access policy creation or modification` fires within the MTTD budget.
ABIOC `Conditional-access policy weakened off the learned admin-change baseline` fires on the same actor.

test_cases.objective: The 'Azure mailbox rule creation' Analytics alert (and the external-forwarding ABIOC) fire on an external auto-forwarding inbox rule, and correlation CR-ITDR-0019 stitches both legs into one incident.
preconditions: The Microsoft 365 audit source is ingesting into msft_o365_audit.
The conditional-access weakening from TC-ITDR-019A occurred on the same identity within the correlation window.
steps: Run azure_audit_emitter to stream a New-InboxRule with an external ForwardTo target.
Observe the mailbox-rule Analytics alert and the external-forwarding ABIOC fire.
Confirm correlation CR-ITDR-0019 raises one stitched Azure identity-persistence incident.
success_criteria: Analytics `Azure mailbox rule creation` fires within the MTTD budget.
ABIOC `External mailbox forwarding rule off the learned inbox-rule baseline` fires on the same mailbox.
Correlation `CR-ITDR-0019` raises exactly one stitched incident.

preventive_controls: Protect conditional-access policy administration behind privileged-identity-management (PIM) just-in-time elevation and require approval for CA policy changes.
Block or alert on Exchange Online mailbox rules that forward or redirect to external recipients (transport-rule guardrail + external-forwarding disabled by default).
Enforce phishing-resistant MFA for all identities that can modify conditional-access policy.
detection_engineering: Baseline which identities and service principals normally modify conditional-access policy and at what cadence; alert on off-baseline CA update/delete operations.
Alert on any inbox rule creation whose ForwardTo/RedirectTo target is an external domain, especially when it closely follows a conditional-access change by the same identity.
Correlate the CA-weakening and mailbox-rule legs on the shared initiating identity within a short window to raise a single high-confidence persistence incident.
